snippet.title: 13 Survival Tools You Should Stockpile Before They’re Gone
snippet.description:
What emergency tools would you want to have at home before a major outage, disaster, or supply shortage begins?

In this video, we cover 13 practical survival and preparedness tools that can become harder to find when everyone suddenly starts preparing at once.

From heavy-duty can openers, ferro rods, headlamps, and manual saws to cast iron cookware, emergency radios, solar charging equipment, pressure canners, pry bars, and manual grain mills, these tools can help with lighting, cooking, communication, repairs, food storage, and long-term preparedness.

You’ll also see why getting the right tools before an emergency happens can save you from scrambling through crowded stores afterward. We’ll break down which items are worth prioritizing first, including affordable essentials you can start with on a limited budget.

The goal isn't to buy everything at once. It’s to build a practical collection of tools that can still be useful when electricity, stores, or normal services aren't available.

Disclaimer: This video is for informational and educational purposes only. Emergency needs vary by location and situation. Always follow official emergency guidance and manufacturer safety instructions, especially when using fire, cutting, canning, electrical, or other specialized equipment.

snippet.title: We Were 17 Floors Up When a 7.7 Earthquake Hit Panama
snippet.description:
What happens when you're traveling the world in retirement and suddenly have nowhere to live? We were 17 floors up in a Panama Airbnb when a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck—and discovered just how much we hadn't planned for.

We'd spent months preparing for full-time retirement travel. We researched visas, healthcare, insurance, budgets, and what to pack. But we hadn't really considered what would happen if an emergency forced us out of our accommodations and we couldn't go back.

Our Ring camera captured the earthquake as it happened. But getting out of the building was only the beginning.

With our dog Brody beside us, we had to make decisions about where to go, how to find reliable information in a foreign country, and where we would spend the night. Businesses were closed, essential medication was left behind, and our belongings were still seventeen floors up in a building that hadn't been cleared for us to return.

In this episode, we share what actually happened, the unexpected kindness of people who helped us, the decisions we got right, and what we wish we'd done differently.

More importantly, we talk about what this experience taught us about retiring abroad, full-time travel, emergency preparedness, and the importance of having a backup plan.

If you're considering slow travel, spending extended periods overseas, or selling your home to travel the world in retirement, these are lessons worth thinking about before you leave.

snippet.title: When the Grid Dies, Your House Fails at 9 Points — in This Exact Order
snippet.description:
The power grid dies and never comes back. Your house starts failing in a specific order — nine points, beginning within the first 24 hours. This is the full sequence, and how to slow it down.

Most preppers plan for food, water, and security. But in a long-term grid-down scenario, the first system to fail is the shelter itself. This video walks through one full year without power and breaks down exactly how a modern house dies — and why the order never changes.

You'll see the sump pump failure that floods basements within 24 hours of a blackout, why a sealed modern home traps moisture until mold takes over (and FEMA's 48-hour rule for stopping it), why pipes still freeze and split even with the water shut off, how a wood stove builds the ice dam that breaches your roof from below, and the small puddle of water that is the only thing standing between your living room and sewer gas.

Every failure point comes with both sides of the card: what accelerates the damage, and the cheap, low-tech moves that slow it down — battery backup pumps, cross-ventilation, RV antifreeze, a roof rake, hardware cloth, and the one habit that kept houses inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone standing for forty years while identical houses next door collapsed into the ground.

If your plan is to bug in, your house is your most important piece of survival gear. Treat this as the maintenance manual for the end of the world.

Safety note: never run unvented combustion heaters indoors — carbon monoxide risks are covered in the video.

snippet.title: Hurricane ISAIAS Prep In Freeport Fl Walton County
snippet.description:
Prepping our house for Hurricane Isaias! We definitely didn’t think we’d be getting ready for a hurricane this week, but here we are.

Thankfully, our house came with Kevlar hurricane window protection, hurricane cables anchored into the foundation, and hurricane straps attached to the roof trusses. Feeling extra grateful for those features right about now!

If you’re buying a home in Freeport, DeFuniak Springs, Santa Rosa Beach, or along 30A, these are some of the things worth asking about. How is the roof connected to the walls? How is the home anchored? Does it have impact-rated windows or other approved storm protection? And what does the wind mitigation report say?

Buying a home in Florida means thinking beyond the pretty kitchen and the backyard. You also want to understand how your home is built to handle our weather.

We’re getting everything secured, praying Isaias weakens and everyone stays safe, and hoping the storm brings some much-needed attention and funding for beach restoration and renourishment along our beautiful Emerald Coast.

Stay safe, everyone! How are you preparing your home?

snippet.title: 13 Must-Have Survival Tools To STOCKPILE Before Anyone Else Does Tools
snippet.description:
Which emergency tools should you have before a major outage or disaster hits? This video breaks down 15 practical hardware-store items that can become difficult to find when everyone starts preparing at the same time.

From heavy-duty can openers, ferro rods, headlamps and manual saws to cast iron cookware, emergency radios, solar charging systems, pressure canners, pry bars and manual grain mills, we look at the tools that can help with lighting, cooking, water storage, repairs, communication and long-term food preparedness.

You'll also learn why buying these items before an emergency can matter more than rushing to the store afterward, plus a simple way to prioritize the cheapest essentials first.

Disclaimer: This video is for informational and educational purposes only. Emergency needs vary by location and situation. Follow official emergency guidance and manufacturer safety instructions, especially when using fire, cutting, canning or other specialized equipment.
